prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface;peak/off-peak/engineering. Operations Control Centre/Line Traffic Controller declares degraded mode for untrusted communications/authority/localization/points/platform-interface;restricts movement. Restoration requires trusted communications,verified positions/routes,maintenance handback,explicit departure restoration,cybersecurity clearance. Signal Maintenance Engineer confirms safety status;resets require engineer/controller concurrence. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restricted-manual movement;Revenue Train Operator repeats restrictions/reports hazards;voice cannot replace validation. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern),non-vital:receives Crew Login Token Bundle;reconciles closures/crowding/deviations;displays faults/restrictions without obscuring alarms;no maintenance commands. Service Timetable Server supplies schedules/platform-context;Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled predictions/patterns/platforms/states;destination/skip-stop requires CBTC identity/route confirmation. North District Zone Controller(Marble) validates Temporary Speed Restriction Notice;South District Zone Controller(Orchid) inhibits automatic routing during manual occupancy-confirmation. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking retain locking/release authority;report points/occupancy/locks. Authority requires locked points,overlap/flank/conflict protection,boundary vacancy. Falcon holds points pending verified release;sends Axle Counter Reset Request;routes/approaches inhibit reset;Maple(unidentified) verifies clearance. West rejects manual-protection conflicts;produces Route Release Exception List. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel):initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout/restricted-manual;enforces authority/speed/doors/braking;produces Brake Curve Checksum Log/berth/door-side/readiness. Cyber Security Officer continuously monitors Safety Data Communication Network,Wayside Radio Access Network,Lantern;correlates authentication failures/session resets/rejections/configuration/timing without altering safety paths;uses audit file for continuity/completeness. Alerts classify impact/territory/authority-risk;notify controller of automatic-operation/communications restrictions. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance controls operational certificates:issuance requires approved identity/software-baseline/domain/service-authorization;renew before expiry for Kestrel,Train Radio Modem,Marble,Orchid,West. Falcon rejects invalid signatures/expired certificates/out-of-window sequences. Revoke compromised/retired/configuration-unreconciled devices. Maintenance Diagnostic Server cannot bypass trust. Appliance administration requires named accounts/MFA/separated

New part:
S218: Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.
S219: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
S220: The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
S221: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
S222: The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.
S223: Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
S224: Commissioning shall begin only after the installed equipment baseline for the Atlas Onboard Controller, Dual Channel Odometer, Train Radio Modem, and wayside control equipment has been configuration checked against the approved release record.
S225: The test-train phase shall use non-passenger movements to prove train localization, movement authority processing, braking response, radio continuity, and operator displays under controlled operating conditions.
S226: Each test train shall be crewed by a Revenue Train Operator qualified for commissioning duties and supported by a Line Traffic Controller with authority to stop the trial when observed conditions depart from the approved script.
S227: Initial movements shall be conducted at restricted commissioning speeds and shall progress to representative service speeds only after the Atlas Onboard Controller and North District Zone Controller demonstrate stable supervision.
S228: The South District Zone Controller shall be commissioned under the same test regime so that boundary behavior is verified before whole-line operation is attempted.
S229: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking shall remain under enhanced monitoring during migration because route setting, point detection, and authority release behavior are critical to mixed-mode operation.
S230: The staged migration from legacy signalling shall divide the railway into controlled areas that can be commissioned, operated, and, if necessary, returned to legacy control without affecting uncommissioned areas.
S231: Cutover planning shall define the exact control boundaries, permissible train movements, staffing levels, and rollback conditions for each migration stage.
S232: Before any cutover stage, the Safety Data Communication Network and Wayside Radio Access Network shall be verified for coverage, latency, redundancy, and alarm presentation at the control center.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
